cells.tense: You are holding the feeling in the room right now, and you have not looked away.
cells.ask: When one person's feeling rises today, stay with it for two full minutes without fixing anything or leaving the room.
cells.core:
You stay in the room when someone near you is upset. Their feeling doesn't swallow you and you don't walk out on it — you keep contact while they have it in front of you. That's the space between two people being kept open and live.

It isn't dramatic and it isn't scripted. Most of what makes it work is that you don't leave and you don't rush in to solve. So today, when one person's feeling comes up, stay with it for two minutes and let it run. No fixing, no exit. Being there through the middle of it is the whole of what you're doing, and you don't need a response ready to do it.
cells.sheetLine: When feeling rises, you stay in the room and hold it.
cells.verb: Holding what people feel and tending the space between them
cells.place: Where something is growing and needs tending, not forcing

cells.tense: You keep planning how you'll carry what they'll feel before anyone has felt it.
cells.ask: This week, when you catch yourself carrying something nobody has told you yet, set it down and say once that you're not sure they'll need you for that.
cells.core:
You're out ahead of feelings that haven't arrived — bracing for the hurt you can see three months off, the breakup that may not happen, the need that hasn't been spoken. You've made room for what someone might want before they've asked, and a lot of what you carry was never going to be needed and goes unused.

What all the bracing can't do is let people meet you where they actually are. So set down one load that hasn't been handed to you, and say once that you're not sure they'll need you for it. Their part stays theirs. You're still there for whatever is real, and being there from now is different from being there early.

cells.tense: The offering of what you feel stopped at some point, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Say one unpolished true sentence about how you feel to one person this week — thirty seconds, no preamble, done before you can smooth it.
cells.core:
The people around you get your practicality and your reliability and your fixing — everything except the feeling itself. You feel plenty. It just isn't coming out of you into the room, and the space between you and other people runs cool and safe and a little empty because of it.

What's absent isn't more feeling pushed at anyone. It's a small true signal from your own side. So say one plain sentence to one person this week about what you feel — thirty seconds, no warm-up, out before you can edit it. Naming it can come afterward. The saying is the part that's been stuck.

cells.tense: You are steadying the room right now while calling it something else.
cells.ask: Name one going thing you did to keep a relationship steady this week and say plainly that you did it.
cells.core:
You're doing the steadying all the time — sitting with someone until they calm down, smoothing what went wrong, keeping two people off each other's throats. It works. Someone lands softer because you were there, and that contact between you is real whether or not it gets named.

But it comes out of your mouth as if it just happened, or as if you were only being useful, as though it had no author. So pick one moment this week where you kept a relationship steady and say plainly that you did that. Nothing gets smaller when you own it — same hands, more awake to them. Not changing what you do. Standing behind it.
